questions.stem:
Passage: I was standing on the edge of a bungee platform, peering down from the height of a 22-storey (83 m) building at a sliver of a stream meandering through a deep valley. I could hear the jump master faintly over the strong wind. "Do not look down. Here we go... one, two, three... jump!" The next thing I knew, I was in a free fall, hurtling down, heading straight towards the boulders. The wind drowned out my scream and just when it felt like a never-ending descent, there was a sharp pull at my body harness and my fall was broken. As I swung, suspended head down, I let the gurgling stream and the tranquil hills calm me. Back at the platform, loud cheers greeted me, even from those I had met only a few minutes earlier. This is what an adventure trip does - strengthens old bonds, creates new ones and helps you challenge yourself! Considered an extreme adventure sport, bungee jumping requires you to free fall from a high structure with an elastic cord attached to your ankles. There are just a handful of activities or sports that can match the thrill of walking to the edge of a precipice and throwing yourself to the winds, but it is essential that you bungee jump only with a certified professional who meets all standard safety regulations. Says an ex-army captain and managing director of Jumpin Heights in Rishikesh, "The biggest challenge of setting up a bungee jumping platform is the apprehension that people have about safety". Where bungee-jumping thrills you with a free fall journey through space, spelunking leads you to the mystical expanse within, and sometimes even under terra firma! An adventure sport that can double up as a means of scientific and archaeological research, spelunking can transport you to a world within a world, with prehistoric rock formations, hidden streams and waterfalls, and more. Also known as caving, the sport is relatively new to India. Essential equipment includes nylon ropes, climbing harness, ascenders and descenders, ladder, scaling pole and hard hat/helmet with a chinstrap. Contrary to common perception, spelunking can be fairly low-risk, depending on the cave you choose. It is always best to go caving in a group of three or more and not alone, and people with respiratory and/or orthopaedic issues are advised to avoid the sport altogether. It is important to remember that there are various forms of life in a cave - from spiders and bats to rare plants and fish species - and you must be careful not to hamper their natural habitat during your sojourn. One of the most popular adventure sports in the world, scuba diving is all about discovering a new habitat and giving in to the spirit of wonder. It is important to note, however, that scuba certification involves a lot of classroom work and in-water practice before an actual dive. A basic understanding of the equipment, diving safety, air and air pressure, and the physics of the activity is essential. Once you exit the bubble of basic scuba training, a world of different types of diving opens up to you - your next tryst with the sport could see you diving from a dive boat, shore diving from a sandy beach or even an inland lake.

Question: Which one of the following is true of the narrator's (bungee jumper) 'leap of faith'?
options: He had no fear as he went down.
His scream was subdued by the wind.
Suspended head down, he could touch the gurgling water.
His fall was towards the plain terrain.
questions.explanation: The passage says the wind drowned out his scream. He let the stream calm him but did not touch it, and the fall was towards boulders.

questions.stem:
Passage: A strange culture of criticism pervades life these days, where everyone is a critic setting sights on errors and indiscretions, more than on achievements and triumphs. Time was when you waited for that one movie or restaurant review from an established media reviewer. Today, thanks to social media, self-appointed critics deluge you with opinions and ratings. Everyone has a view on where the PM is going wrong and what his next step should be. A minister or godman just has to open his mouth before the media pounces and makes it a matter of national debate, involving wilting insults and shattering downers. With eyes trained on indiscretions, we ignore achievements and recognition. We have become a nation that loves having an opinion, preferably negative; and likes nothing better than sharing it. It is indeed a voyeuristic, sadistic generation that takes pleasure in the downfall and public disgrace of others. In a terrible about-turn of the phrase 'no-news-is-good-news', today, we have come to a stage when 'good-news-is-no news'. Media leads the charge, each TV channel watching out for 'Breaking News' moments - mostly censoring or condemning a perceived wrong move, a misdirected word or action, a wardrobe malfunction or the mouthing of a dirty word on the cricket field. People invariably tweet negative stuff, easily adopting moral grandstands, because that is what catches attention. Egged on by a trigger-happy audio-visual media, which shoots down and ridicules public figures for the slightest gaffe, we are stepping into a well-established culture of the Tall Poppy Syndrome! (A social phenomenon where those with more merit or success are disparaged and pulled down). It is all very well for children to pull each other down under the keen pressure of performance, dismissing achievers as 'nerds' and 'losers'. It is even understandable when professionals do so in a dog-eat-dog world, where pulling down one may spell success for another. But when the habit of condemnation and fault-finding becomes a national pastime, we need to sound the danger bells. Children today tune into news channels not for information, but to guffaw at people pulling each other down. The more vitriolic the content, the higher the TRPs a programme delivers. Forgetting to praise the good work done, bosses pounce on little mistakes. Experience tells us that positive strokes work far better than ridicule, especially public ridicule. Today, we have the power to make and break people through exposes and sting operations. But we also still retain the power to motivate and galvanise the good amongst us. When we criticise, let us also stay attuned to the good in those we deride.

Question: Why does the author say 'a strange culture of criticism has pervaded...'?
options: Criticism is done through the social media which is a new channel of communication.
The author is averse to criticism and hence calls it 'strange'.
Ours has been a different culture in the world for centuries and centuries.
Not long ago we used to appreciate many good things and achievements that happened around us; now it is not so.
questions.explanation: The opening contrasts the present, when everyone looks for errors, with the past, when reviews and achievements were recognised.

C. I want to distinguish between being just literate and being knowledgeable.
D. Essentially, the when and why of it.
questions.explanation: C sets the theme, A gives the farmer example, D ('the when and why') explains understanding, B adds the weather forecast.

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. Lymphoma can easily spread throughout the body, so patients whose disease appears to be confined to one or a few lymph nodes may have collections of cancerous cells elsewhere in the body that are not big enough to be detected by the tests used in staging the disease.
B. Treatment of lymphoma is tailored to each individual patient, depending on the type of lymphoma present, how fast it grows, and how far it has spread.
C. In general, lymphomas that derive from 'T' cells are more difficult to treat than 'B' cell lymphomas, and patients aged over 60 are less likely to be cured than younger patients.
D. For this reason, the treatment of choice for lymphoma is usually chemotherapy - drugs given by mouth or through the veins to destroy the rapidly proliferating cancer cells throughout the body.
questions.explanation: 'For this reason' in D must follow the spread described in A. B and C describe treatment variation and come first.

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. Official records show that the gross enrolment rate in higher education is only 11 per cent while the National Knowledge Commission says that only seven per cent of the population between the age group of 18-24 enters higher education.
B. Experts acknowledge that the present higher education system in India is not equipped to address the problem of shortage of skilled manpower and requires some changes in the basic structure.
C. Even those who have access are not ensured of quality.
D. The shortage of skilled manpower is a cause for concern in most sectors in India.
questions.explanation: D states the problem, B gives the experts' view, A gives access figures, C adds that even those with access lack quality.

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. One of the main reasons for industrial sickness in our country has been the fact that business and industrial managers have not been able to look beyond the immediate future.
B. The planning horizon has hardly ever exceeded five years.
C. A leading Indian industrialist in an article on ways to strengthen India's economy has drawn attention to the problems of inflation and industrial sickness among other things.
D. They have been too preoccupied with their attempts to report favourable results for the current year - higher profits and larger dividends to the shareholders.
questions.explanation: C introduces the article, A gives the reason, D ('They') explains the managers' preoccupation, B adds the short planning horizon.

questions.stem:
Choose the most logical order of sentences to construct a coherent paragraph.
A. A Standing Committee in the Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (DIPP) will oversee the implementation of this order and will further make recommendations to nodal ministries and procuring entities.
B. The new policy will boost domestic manufacturing and service provision, and enhance income and employment.
C. The policy aims to maintain the balance between promoting 'Make in India' and ensuring timely supply of good quality and value-for-money products to the procuring government entities.
D. The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister has given its approval for a national procurement policy that gives preference to 'Make in India' in government procurements.
questions.explanation: D announces the policy, C states its aim, B its benefits, A who will oversee implementation.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks. With more and more uncommon policies, you can insure anything from your ______ to your ______.
questions.explanation: 'From your pet to your toe' fits 'uncommon policies'. Life, house and vehicle are common insurance.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks. The ______ of the job made him do his work ______.
questions.explanation: Monotony of the job leads to doing work perfunctorily (without care).

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks. The retired judge was too ______ to be taken in by the spurious excuses presented by the ______ crook.
questions.explanation: A wise (sagacious) judge is not fooled by the excuses of an ingenious (clever) crook. This question was flagged by the candidate and the key is not confirmed.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks. The spirit of sportsmanship is, in fact, the ______ of all maladies that ______ the world today.
questions.explanation: A panacea is a cure for all ills; maladies afflict the world.

questions.stem: Fill in the blanks. In today's public ______, scientists are highly respected but not nearly as influential as they should be; their voices are mostly ______ in the arena of public policy.
questions.explanation: 'Public domain' and 'marginalised voices' fit the contrast between respect and influence.

questions.stem: Identify the best way of writing the sentence ensuring that the message being conveyed remains the same.
options: Said to be on the verge of extinction, a great deal of attention is attracted by Olive Ridley turtle from conservationists and the media.
Said to be on the verge of extinction, the conservationists and the media are giving a great deal of attention to Olive Ridley turtle.
Said to be on the verge of extinction, the Olive Ridley turtle is attracting the conservationists and the media to a great deal of attention.
Said to be on the verge of extinction, the Olive Ridley turtle attracts a great deal of attention from conservationists and the media.
questions.explanation: The opening phrase must modify the turtle. Only option 4 puts 'the Olive Ridley turtle' right after it.

questions.stem: Identify the best way of writing the sentence ensuring that the message being conveyed remains the same.
options: The recent change in the Quarterly's book-review is short-sighted and self-defeating.
The change of late in the Quarterly's book-review is short-sighted and self-defeating.
The recent change in the Quarterly's book-review is short-sighted and also is self-deprecating.
The change that has been made recently in the Quarterly's book-review is short-sighted and self-defeating.
questions.explanation: Option A is concise and idiomatic. 'Self-deprecating' is the wrong word, and options 2 and 4 are wordy.

questions.stem: Identify the best way of writing the sentence ensuring that the message being conveyed remains the same.
options: Whoever leaves the room last is requested for locking the door after him.
Whomever leaves the room last is requested to lock the door after him.
Whoever leaves the room last is requested to lock the door after him.
Whomever leaves the room last is requested for locking the door after him.
questions.explanation: 'Whoever' is the subject of 'leaves' (nominative), and 'requested to lock' is the correct construction.

questions.stem: Identify the best way of writing the sentence ensuring that the message being conveyed remains the same.
options: His son carried off his business after his demise.
His son carried on his business after his demise.
His son carried out his business after his demise.
His son carried away his business after his demise.
questions.explanation: 'Carry on' = continue.

questions.stem: Identify the best way of writing the sentence ensuring that the message being conveyed remains the same.
options: He will not pay unless he is compelled to.
He will not pay unless he will be compelled.
He will not pay unless he is not compelled.
He will not pay till he is compelled to.
questions.explanation: After 'unless' we use the present tense, and the sentence already carries a negative so 'not compelled' is wrong.

questions.stem: Each of these questions consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) He was able to (2) complete the book (3) by planning carefully (4) and worked diligently.
questions.explanation: Parallel structure: 'by planning carefully and working diligently'.

questions.stem: Each of these questions consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) When the rudder (2) broke off from the boat, (3) the sailor jumped in the bay (4) and swam to the shore.
options: the sailor jumped in the bay
questions.explanation: 'Jumped into the bay' shows motion; 'in' shows location.

questions.stem: Each of these questions consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) The current edition (2) of the encyclopaedia, (3) which I saw yesterday, (4) said that cloning is possible.
questions.explanation: The current edition states a fact that is still true, so the present tense 'says' is expected. The key is not confirmed.

questions.stem: Each of these questions consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) The loss of three friends (2) and a job (3) were the price Patel had to pay (4) for his ill tempered outbursts.
options: were the price Patel had to pay
questions.explanation: The complement 'the price' is singular, so 'was the price' is expected. The key is not confirmed (the subject could be read as plural).

questions.stem: Each of these questions consists of a sentence divided into four parts numbered (1) to (4). Only one part is not acceptable in standard written English. Identify the part which contains an error. (1) In the new school, (2) the teachers (3) were more friendly (4) than my old school.
questions.explanation: Illogical comparison: teachers must be compared with teachers: 'than those in my old school'.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. Harold was an excellent husband - tender, thoughtful, proud and affectionate; he was irreproachable.
questions.explanation: Irreproachable = blameless; impeachable = open to blame or accusation.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. Boozy, brawling and bold; he is excoriated by the right wing for his opposition to the Vietnam War.
questions.explanation: Excoriated = severely criticised; commended = praised. 'Reviled' is a synonym.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. The boy jumped up and down with alacrity as he inched closer to the candy store.
questions.explanation: Alacrity = eager readiness; apathy = lack of interest.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. She had been ready with a flow of wrathful expostulation, but suddenly she burst into tears.
questions.explanation: Wrathful = angry; calm is the opposite.

questions.stem: Choose the alternative which is closest to the opposite in meaning of the underlined word in the sentence. Yet this ungainly exterior sheltered a tender, romantic and idealistic soul.
questions.explanation: Ungainly = clumsy; graceful is the true opposite. 'Attractive' is about looks, not movement.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. The Puritan elders tried to ban levity of all sorts from the community meetings.
questions.explanation: Levity = lack of seriousness, frivolity.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. I have my fingers in too many pies, I am completely frazzled.
questions.explanation: Frazzled = worn out.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. It is hard to locate the roots of peripatetic gypsies and their borrowed traditions.
questions.explanation: Peripatetic = travelling from place to place, itinerant.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. The audience had no problem understanding the presenter's perspicuous speech.
questions.explanation: Perspicuous = clearly expressed, lucid.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the alternative which can replace the underlined word without changing the meaning of the sentence. He acquiesced to his son's decision to go out without an umbrella despite the prediction of rain.
questions.explanation: Acquiesce = accept reluctantly without protest, submit.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. An extremely confused or complicated situation
questions.explanation: Imbroglio = a confusing, complicated situation. Oppugn means to oppose.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A formal resignation and renunciation of powers
questions.explanation: Abdication = formally giving up the throne or power.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A person who hates reason or discussion
questions.explanation: Misologist = a hater of reason or argument. A misogynist hates women; a misanthropist hates mankind.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. A child who stays away from school without leave or explanation
questions.explanation: Truant = one who skips school without permission.

questions.stem: In each of these questions, choose the option which can be substituted for the given words/sentence. To express vehement protest
questions.explanation: Fulminate = to protest loudly and angrily.

questions.stem: The judges of Supreme Court hold office till they reach the age of ______.
questions.explanation: Under Article 124(2), a Supreme Court judge holds office until 65 years of age.

questions.stem: Which one of the following committees was constituted in the year 1991 for reforms in tax structure in India?
questions.explanation: The Tax Reforms Committee (1991-93) was chaired by Raja Chelliah. The Narasimham Committee dealt with the financial sector.

questions.stem: In India, the Tropic of Cancer does not pass through which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.stem: The axis of the earth is stated to be inclined at an angle of 66.5 degrees. With respect to which of the following does the axis of the earth form this angle?
questions.explanation: The axis makes 66.5 degrees with the plane of the earth's orbit (the ecliptic).

questions.stem: The Indira Gandhi Canal originates from which one of the following?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi (Rajasthan) Canal starts at the Harike Barrage at the confluence of the Sutlej and Beas.

questions.stem: The process of photosynthesis is most active in the ______ regions of the spectrum.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light most strongly.

questions.stem: Inside the human body, blood does not coagulate due to the presence of ______.
questions.explanation: Heparin is a natural anticoagulant.

questions.stem: In the case of a deadlock between the two houses of the Parliament of India, on a legislative measure the joint sitting is presided over by the:
options: A member of Lok Sabha specifically elected for the purpose
questions.explanation: Under Article 108 the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting.

questions.stem: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country by area. (Mongolia is second-largest of the landlocked countries and is often mistaken for it.)

questions.stem: Every year, International Cancer Day is observed on ______.
questions.explanation: World Cancer Day is 4 February.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice and not more than ______ other Judges appointed by the President of India.
questions.explanation: In 2017 the number was 30 other judges. Note: since the 2019 amendment it is 33, so this item is outdated.

questions.stem: Who has been elected as the 18th Prime Minister of Pakistan by the National Assembly after the resignation of Nawaz Sharif?
questions.explanation: Shahid Khaqan Abbasi became PM in August 2017.

questions.stem: The senior Indian lawyer who argued for India in the hearing at the International Court of Justice on the Kulbhushan Jadhav case is:
questions.explanation: Harish Salve represented India at the ICJ.

questions.stem: ______ who passed away in May 2017, was the first woman to become Chief Justice of a High Court in India.
questions.explanation: Leila Seth was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court (Himachal Pradesh).

questions.stem: Which of the following Mughal emperors defeated the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodhi, in 1526 at Panipat to capture Delhi and Agra?
questions.explanation: Babur won the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

questions.stem: The principal seat of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh is located in which one of the following cities?
questions.explanation: The MP High Court's principal seat is Jabalpur, with benches at Indore and Gwalior.

questions.stem: Who among the following has been appointed as the Chairman of the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) in August 2017 by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India?
questions.explanation: Prasoon Joshi replaced Pahlaj Nihalani in August 2017.

questions.stem: The Indian National Congress adopted a resolution at its historic ______ session in 1929 calling for 'Purna Swaraj' from the British.
questions.explanation: The Lahore session (1929) under Jawaharlal Nehru declared Purna Swaraj.

questions.stem: In which district of Karnataka is the historic place 'Hampi' located?
questions.explanation: Hampi is in Ballari (Bellary) district.

questions.stem: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr Rajendra Prasad was the permanent President; Sachchidananda Sinha was the temporary president. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

questions.stem: The most famous musician at the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar was Tansen. His original name was:
questions.explanation: Tansen's birth name was Ramtanu Pandey.

questions.stem: The electrical equivalent of one horse power is equal to ______ in the International System of Unit (SI)?
Who among the following athletes has won the men's 100 metres sprint at the recently concluded IAAF World Athletics Championships in London?
questions.explanation: Justin Gatlin won the 2017 men's 100 m. Coleman was second and Bolt third.

questions.stem: Where will India and the USA be co-hosting the Global Entrepreneurship Summit in November 2017?
questions.explanation: GES 2017 was held in Hyderabad.

questions.stem: The Reserve Bank of India has recently introduced Rs 50 denomination banknotes in the Mahatma Gandhi Series with motif of ______ on the reverse.
questions.explanation: The new Rs 50 note shows Hampi with Chariot.

questions.stem: A group of friends met at a club 15 days ago and promised to meet again after 36 days. If today is Saturday, on which day will the friends meet again?
questions.explanation: Meeting is 36 - 15 = 21 days from today, which is a multiple of 7, so it is Saturday.

questions.stem: In a certain code, SAM is written as 917 and ENTHUSE is written as 2634892. In this coding system, which of the following could be a possible code for the word ENTHUSIASM?
questions.explanation: S=9, A=1, M=7, E=2, N=6, T=3, H=4, U=8. ENTHUSIASM = 2 6 3 4 8 9 I 1 9 7, and only option 1 fits.

questions.stem: Find the sum of all two-digit numbers that give a remainder of 3 when they are divided by 7.
A mixture worth Rs 3.25 a kg is formed by mixing two types of rice, one costing Rs 3.10 per kg and the other Rs 3.60. In what proportion must they have been mixed?
Typist P can type a sheet in 6 minutes, typist Q in 7 minutes and typist R in 9 minutes. The average number of sheets typed per hour per typist if all three typists are typing, is ______.
questions.explanation: Sheets per hour: 10, 60/7, 20/3. Sum = 530/21; average = 530/63.

questions.stem: Find the selling price of goods if two salesmen claim to make 25% profit each, one calculating it on cost price and the other on the selling price; the difference in the profits earned being Rs 100 and selling price being the same in both the cases.
questions.explanation: Profit on SP = 0.25 SP; on CP = 0.2 SP. Difference 0.05 SP = 100, so SP = 2000.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper sells rice in such a way that the selling price of 950 gm is the same as the cost price of one kilogram. Find his gain percent.

A salesman is appointed on a basic salary of Rs 1200 per month and the condition that for sales of Rs 10000 or above, he will get 50% of the basic salary and 10% of the sale values as a reward. This incentive scheme does not operate for the first Rs 10000 of sales. What should be the value of sales if he wants to earn Rs 7600 in a particular month?
questions.explanation: 1200 + 600 + 10% of (S - 10000) = 7600 gives S = 68,000, which is not among the options.

questions.stem: Rana makes a deposit of Rs 50000 for a period of 2.5 years in the ACB Bank. If the rate of interest is 12% per annum compounded half-yearly, find the maturity value of the money (approx.) deposited by him.
questions.explanation: 5 half-year periods at 6%: 50000 x 1.06^5 = 66,911.

questions.stem: The students in three batches of BBA are in the ratio 2:3:5. If 20 students are increased in each batch, the ratio changes to 4:5:7. The total number of students in the three batches taken together, before the increase, is ______.
In a certain city, there are four men for every three women and five children for every three men. How many children are there in the city if it has 531 women?
If the price of a commodity is raised by 10%, find out by how much per cent must a householder reduce his consumption of that commodity, so as not to increase his expenditure.
Find the compound interest on Rs 50000 for 3 years if the rate of interest is 5% for the first year, 6% for the second year and 10% for the third year.
A train 100 m long is running at a speed of 70 km per hour. In how much time will it pass a man who is running at 10 km per hour in the same direction in which the train is going?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 60 km/h = 50/3 m/s. Time = 100 / (50/3) = 6 s.

questions.stem: Two partners invest Rs 87000 and Rs 72500 respectively, in a business and agree that 25% of the profit should be divided equally between them and the remaining profit is to be treated as interest on capital. If one partner gets Rs 240 more than the other, find the total profit made in the business.
questions.explanation: Capital ratio 6:5. The equal part cancels; 0.75 P x 1/11 = 240, so P = 3520.

questions.stem: If the letters 'Q B Z H X H Q D U M B' are placed in the order opposite to the one in which these normally appear in the English alphabet (i.e. in reverse order), then which of these would be the fifth letter from right to left?
questions.explanation: Reverse alphabetical order: Z X U Q Q M H H D B B. Fifth from the right is H.

questions.stem: Soham says, "I have as many sisters as brothers". Pooja says, "Each of us sisters has only half as many sisters as brothers". Assuming that Soham and Pooja are brother and sister, how many brothers and sisters does the family have?
questions.explanation: Let brothers = b, sisters = s. Soham: s = b - 1. Pooja: s - 1 = b/2. So b = 4, s = 3.

questions.stem: Which one of the following does not belong to the series? Abz, Bcy, Cdx, Dew, Efr
questions.explanation: The pattern is next letter, next letter, previous letter: Efv would follow. 'Efr' breaks it.

questions.stem: A pizza delivery boy started walking southwards to reach his destination which is 6 kms away. From the target, after delivering the pizza, he turns 180 degrees in the clockwise direction and then turns 45 degrees in the anti-clockwise direction. Which direction is he facing now from his destination?
questions.explanation: Facing south, a 180 degree turn makes him face north. Turning 45 degrees anticlockwise from north makes him face north-west.

questions.stem: Neeta is teaching relations to her daughter. She says, "How is my mother's mother's daughter-in-law's daughter related to me?" What will be the correct relationship?
questions.explanation: Mother's mother's daughter-in-law is Neeta's maternal uncle's wife, and her daughter is Neeta's cousin.

questions.stem:
Read the following information: There are five villages A, B, C, D and E. Two of these have post offices, three have schools and three are accessible by road. Two have population of more than 5000 each, two have population between 2000 and 5000 each and one has a population of less than 2000. Two of these villages have electricity in addition to certain other facilities such as school and accessibility by road. One village with a population of less than 2000 also has a school but neither has a post office nor is accessible by road, while each of the villages with a population of more than 5000 has a school. Of the two villages having population between 2000 and 5000 only one has a post office and is accessible by road. A is accessible by road. B has a population of more than 5000, D has a school and is accessible by road but does not have a post office, while E has a school but is not accessible by road.

Question: Which village does not have any of the facilities available to other villages?
questions.explanation: Working it out: A (2000-5000, post office, road), B (>5000, school, post office, road), D (>5000, school, road), E (<2000, school). C has none of the facilities.

questions.stem:
Read the following information: There are five villages A, B, C, D and E. Two of these have post offices, three have schools and three are accessible by road. Two have population of more than 5000 each, two have population between 2000 and 5000 each and one has a population of less than 2000. Two of these villages have electricity in addition to certain other facilities such as school and accessibility by road. One village with a population of less than 2000 also has a school but neither has a post office nor is accessible by road, while each of the villages with a population of more than 5000 has a school. Of the two villages having population between 2000 and 5000 only one has a post office and is accessible by road. A is accessible by road. B has a population of more than 5000, D has a school and is accessible by road but does not have a post office, while E has a school but is not accessible by road.

Question: Which three villages are accessible by road?
questions.explanation: A, B and D are on the road network; C and E are not.

questions.stem:
Read the following information: There are five villages A, B, C, D and E. Two of these have post offices, three have schools and three are accessible by road. Two have population of more than 5000 each, two have population between 2000 and 5000 each and one has a population of less than 2000. Two of these villages have electricity in addition to certain other facilities such as school and accessibility by road. One village with a population of less than 2000 also has a school but neither has a post office nor is accessible by road, while each of the villages with a population of more than 5000 has a school. Of the two villages having population between 2000 and 5000 only one has a post office and is accessible by road. A is accessible by road. B has a population of more than 5000, D has a school and is accessible by road but does not have a post office, while E has a school but is not accessible by road.

Question: Which village has a population of less than 2000?
questions.explanation: E has a school but no post office and no road, and B and D are the two villages above 5000, so E is the one below 2000.

questions.stem:
A + B means A is the son of B; A - B means A is the wife of B; and A * B means A is the sister of B.
Preetam + Monika - Aloke means ______.
options: Preetam is the grandson of Aloke
Preetam is the grandfather of Aloke
Aloke is the grandmother of Preetam
Preetam is the son of Aloke
questions.explanation: Preetam is the son of Monika, and Monika is the wife of Aloke, so Preetam is Aloke's son.

questions.stem:
A + B means A is the son of B; A - B means A is the wife of B; and A * B means A is the sister of B.
A + B - C + D would mean all of the following except ______.
options: A is the granddaughter of D
D is the father-in-law of B
questions.explanation: A is the son of B and C, and C is D's son, so A is D's grandson, not granddaughter. Statement 3 is also not certain (D's gender is not given), so this key is not confirmed.

questions.stem: In MS-Word, if you want to display the meaning of a word in your text at the bottom of the last page, which feature will help you?
questions.explanation: Endnotes are collected at the end of the document (the last page). Footnotes appear at the bottom of each page. Options 2 and 4 are printed identically in the original paper.

questions.stem: What is the shortcut to add a new slide in MS-PowerPoint?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+M inserts a new slide. Ctrl+N opens a new presentation.

questions.stem: What is the shortcut key to create a copyright symbol in MS-Word?
questions.explanation: Alt+Ctrl+C inserts the (c) symbol via AutoCorrect.

questions.stem: In MS-Excel, what is the keyboard shortcut (button or buttons to be pressed) for creating a chart from the selected cells?
questions.explanation: F11 creates a chart on a new sheet from the selected data.

questions.stem: If we want to open a PowerPoint file in slide show mode directly instead of opening it in PowerPoint and then selecting slide show, in which format should you save the presentation file?
questions.explanation: The .ppsx (PowerPoint Show) format opens straight into slide show mode.

questions.stem: In MS-Excel, if you want to show unique values of a particular column, which feature can help you?
questions.explanation: 'Remove Duplicates' (Data tab) leaves only unique values. There is no 'Show Unique' command. The key is not confirmed (Advanced Filter with 'Unique records only' also does this).

questions.stem: What is the shortcut to increase the font size in MS-Word?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+> steps the font size up. (Ctrl+] also increases it by 1 pt, so this key is not confirmed.)

questions.stem: Which one of the following memory units is considered as the largest?
questions.explanation: Order: PB < EB < ZB < YB.

questions.stem: ______ monitors user activity on internet and transmits that information in the background to someone else.
questions.explanation: Spyware secretly collects and sends user information.

questions.stem: Which tool in MS Excel is used to create headings that spread across multiple columns?
questions.explanation: Merge & Center merges cells across columns.

questions.stem: In MS-Word, when you want to repeat the same formatting at different places in your document, you can take the help of:
questions.explanation: Styles store a set of formatting that can be reused.

questions.stem: DNS is an acronym for ______.
questions.explanation: DNS = Domain Name System.

questions.stem: In MS-Word, which of the following does not fall under paragraph formatting?
questions.explanation: Underline is character (font) formatting.

questions.stem: What does the SUMIF function in MS-Excel do?
options: Adds up cell values based on a condition
Adds all the numbers in a range of cells
Returns a subtotal in a list or database
questions.explanation: SUMIF adds only those cells that meet a given condition. SUM adds all numbers; SUBTOTAL returns subtotals.

questions.stem: To assign a name to locate/reach a specific point in an MS Word document, the user should create a ______.
questions.explanation: A bookmark names a location in a document.

questions.stem: What combination of keys do you press to enter the current date in a cell in MS-Excel?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+; enters today's date; Ctrl+Shift+: enters the current time.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the communication protocol that sets the standard used by every computer that accesses web-based information?
questions.explanation: HTTP is the web's transfer protocol.

questions.stem: What is a gutter margin?
options: Margin that is added to the left margin when printing
Margin that is added to the right margin when printing
Margin that is added to the binding side of the page when printing
Margin that is added to the outside of the page when printing
questions.explanation: A gutter margin adds extra space on the binding side.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct for charts in MS Excel?
options: A chart can have a chart title, legends and axis titles.
A chart can have a chart title and legends but no axis titles.
A chart can have a legends and axis titles but not a chart title.
A chart can have a chart title and axis titles but not legends.
questions.explanation: A chart can have all three elements at once.

questions.stem: If you want to type a character which is not there in the keyboard; for example, the copyright symbol, how will you bring such a character in your text?
options: Purchase a keyboard with all symbols.
questions.explanation: Character Map (or Insert > Symbol) provides special characters.

questions.stem: In MS-Word, which of the following shortcut keys is used to check Spelling and Grammar?
questions.explanation: F7 starts the spelling and grammar check.

questions.stem: What term describes explanatory text attached to a cell in MS-Excel?
questions.explanation: A comment (or note) is explanatory text attached to a cell.

questions.stem: Firewall is a type of ______.
questions.explanation: A firewall is a security tool that filters network traffic; it is not a virus, worm or threat.

questions.stem: ______ is distributed computing over a network, and involves a large number of computers connected via real-time communication network such as the Internet.
questions.explanation: This is the standard definition of cloud computing.

questions.stem: A ______ is a website like any other, but it is intended to offer personal opinions of people on their hobbies, interests, commentaries, photos, etc.
questions.explanation: A blog is a personal-opinion website.
